A 55% refresh reserve every four years plus 3% annual spares is a long-run house allowance, not compulsory retirement at a contract expiry. Post-horizon market growth of 6% for five years is a separate house assumption; new/renewed contracts reprice every three years in that terminal regime.

steady.footer: $5.06m normalized cash per earning IT MW; 3.81× revenue from the shared DCF. The house default adds 0.5×, giving 4.31× revenue.
steady.basis: Horizon revenue per earning IT MW and the actual modeled contract/spot revenue mix feed the shared steady-state DCF. Company running-cost margins and maintenance assumptions are retained. A 55% refresh reserve every four years plus 3% annual spares is a long-run house allowance, not compulsory retirement at a contract expiry. Post-horizon market growth of 6% for five years is a separate house assumption; new/renewed contracts reprice every three years in that terminal regime. Default valuation includes a separate 0.5× house premium above the DCF-derived multiple. All sensitivities vary around this default; the no-premium case remains available.

prepay.basis: 50% of GPU capex on contracted capacity (FY26 release fn.4: 45-55%), credited back after month 24 to the end of term (Microsoft SOW EX-10.3 s3.2.a.iii mechanism); Microsoft $1.933bn = $483m per Horizon: three received by 30 Sep 2026 (deferred lease revenue rose $473m in the September quarter), the fourth carried on Horizon 4 delivery in 2027Q1 because fees, credits and reimbursements are under discussion (10-Q); deferred revenue $2.544bn at 30 Sep 2026 ($2,096m leases + $448m services) is the opening balance, of which ~$1.06bn is other customers; Microsoft credits run over months 25-60 from each Horizon's start (Horizon 1 from 2028Q3, Horizons 2-4 from 2029Q1); the latest five-year contract carries a 90% prepayment but the base stays at 50% Modeled future receipts retain the capex-based funding assumption; they are not secured financing. Inferred credits use modeled service start and contract expiry: after eight service quarters through expiry. Explicit opening-balance credits and special receipts retain their own dated schedules. Mixed future tranches allocate inferred credits by contractual IT MW; purchase capex remains scheduled if delivery slips.

finance.basis: debt 7% (converts 0.9% cash coupon; Microsoft-backed GPU debt SOFR+2.25% and 5.96% notes; the two GPU financings for other customers are 9.0% and 9.51% fixed — two-thirds of backlog is investment-grade, so the blend holds at ~7%), 16%/yr pool amortisation, $3bn cash floor, 10% of capex from 2027 as policy equity at $19.73 (the 10 Nov 2026 mark; October ATM sales averaged ~$36) plus the residual; lenders advance 90% of GPUs and 65% of shell on contracted capacity, 50% on spot; converts (six series, $6.746bn, capped calls, 10-Q) convert only where the model 2030 price clears the strike; balance sheet at 30 Sep 2026 pro forma for the $388m term-loan draw on 1 Oct and ~$630m of October share sales: debt $10.43bn, cash $4.54bn, restricted cash $2.256bn counted; share count 456.1m = 424.36m on the 30 Oct cover + 31.7m restricted stock units (NVIDIA investment rights 30.0m and options 5.1m excluded as out of the money); prepaid forwards 14.5m shares returned Dec-29/Jun-30; discounted 4.14 years from 10 Nov 2026 to end-2030

facts: $10.4bn debt − $4.5bn cash, 30 Sep pro forma October
notes: 5,610 MW announced across nine sites. Land cost $139m — $25k per MW. The value is in the grid connections, not the dirt.10-K Item 2 · Note 14
Sweetwater 1’s substation energised 1 May 2026 — three months before ERCOT froze the queue. Power ramps with construction; 1.4 GW sits inside the moat.8-K 7 May · Governor’s directive 3 Aug

~93 MW earning at 30 September. Horizon 1 (50 MW IT) has billed since Microsoft accepted it in August. Horizons 2–4 are built and powered but bill from January–February 2027: Microsoft asked for a network change across all four, and the contract extends dates without delay credits.Q1 FY27 10-Q · 5 Nov call

The 2026 programme lands a quarter late. The 0.3 GW of IT that was due by December is now targeted for 31 January 2027, possibly end-February; Mackenzie arrives late December or early 2027 and the Childress air-cooled halls are spread across 2027. First revenue moves; the hardware is bought on the original calendar.Q1 FY27 10-Q · deck · call

0.8 GW by December 2027 is unchanged on the company’s schedule: Sweetwater 1’s first 300 MW gross is still targeted for Q4 2027. SemiAnalysis’s site work is later — 158 MW of IT by end-2026, 578 MW by end-2027 and 1.7 GW by end-2028; the page’s earning megawatts sit below those figures in 2026–27.Q1 FY27 deck · SemiAnalysis 3Q26 update
Density rises: 2.9 kW per GB300 package, 3.5–4.7 kW Rubin, 6.3 kW next-gen. Same megawatt, fewer chips, same dollars per MW.model tranches

Contract cohorts. Existing/inferred book keeps its original all-in rate until a disclosed or estimated expiry. Expiry ends signed coverage; continuation becomes an assumed renewal. New capacity uses one shared house curve. IREN’s own prints now bracket the top of it: three-year $19–23m and five-year ~$17m per IT MW-year in the September quarter, then a five-year contract at ~$22m with 90% of the GPU cost prepaid and a short-term one at $40m.Q1 FY27 release · deck

Compare matching measures. Annualized earning contracted revenue divided by earning contracted IT MW measures contract yield. Total annualized revenue divided by all earning IT MW includes spot. Neither denominator should be paired with full energized-capacity ARR.

Evidence. Every tranche records price, commitment and expiry provenance. An inferred allocation is not a verified contract. New prices, zero software premium and 100% same-hardware renewal continuation are explicit assumptions.

“Recent customer prepayments represent 45–55% of GPU capex.” On Microsoft, prepayments plus $3.6bn of investment-grade debt funded ~96% of the GPUs. Backlog is $20.3bn across 15 customers, two-thirds investment-grade. The ATM has sold 29.6m shares since 30 June — 17.4m of them in October at ~$36 — and has $2.3bn left of $6bn.Q1 FY27 10-Q · release

“Our entire data center portfolio is unencumbered today, including Horizons One through four.” Lenders hold the GPUs ($1.49bn pledged, non-recourse) and the Microsoft receivables — not the land, buildings or substations.A. Lewis, CFO, FY26 call · 10-K Note 23

The catch: prepayments and 90% gearing exist only on signed capacity, and the FY27 capex guide has been cut from $25–30bn to ~$20bn — “purely and simply financial markets”. $6bn of the remaining $15bn is not yet funded. Unsigned capacity needs ~$25m of equity per IT MW, or is simply not built.CFO, 5 Nov call · funding stack above

Common calculation, different costs. The steady-state multiple is recomputed from horizon earned revenue per IT MW. Company margins, leased or owned shell costs, maintenance, tax and discount assumptions remain explicit.

Equipment life is separate. A contract expiry does not remove the GPUs or install a newer generation. Existing equipment renews at its own rate; the long-run maintenance reserve is a house assumption.

House default, 15 September 2026. Add 0.5× to the DCF-derived EV/revenue multiple for IREN. This is a valuation judgment, separate from operating cash-flow assumptions. The no-premium case remains available; other sensitivities are measured from the new default.

Reconciled value. Updated quarterly revenue passes through the existing debt, prepayment and dilution waterfall. The terminal multiple is recalculated from the displayed steady-state inputs, plus the separately disclosed 0.5× house premium.

Separate clocks. Pricing policy is dated 15 September 2026. The balance sheet is 30 September 2026, pro forma for October share sales and the 1 October term-loan draw. New equity is issued at the 10 November 2026 market reference, $19.73.

arr.cap: Annualized earned revenue is split into existing book (including estimates), assumed renewals, assumed new contracts and spot. Full-capacity contracted run-rate is a separate measure.

footer.model: Shared pricing and contract-cohort model. Existing commitments, estimated coverage, same-hardware renewals and new business are distinguished. Pricing, expiry and continuity assumptions are exposed with their evidence. Company financing and capex retain the dated research snapshot.

capexBasis: by energisation vintage, $m: GPUs + ancillaries — GB300 liquid $29m (Nov-25 Microsoft/Dell order, 8-K 3-Nov-25), air B300 $31m, +15-20% on 2027 orders (CFO, FY26 call: $36m air, ~$34m liquid), Rubin ~$40m, next-gen ~$45m; shell $15m liquid new-build (Nov-25 deck $14-16m), $5m air retrofit

market.units: USD millions per IT MW per year; all-in contracted services
market.tenorBasis: The initial new-business curve has no calibrated tenor premium or discount. Term controls the next renewal date. A five-year, 15% lower-price case is an explicit sensitivity, not a disclosed market spread.
market.generationBasis: The shared frontier curve is quoted per IT MW, with generation factors of 1 as an explicit house assumption. It is not a hardware productivity forecast. Existing equipment renews at its own all-in price; renewal does not install new GPUs.

renewal.basis: Base assumes the same hardware keeps earning at the original all-in rate and 100% contracted capacity renews. These are house assumptions, not commitments. Price and retention downside cases are shown.

spot.note: Shared realized spot assumptions inherited from the CoreWeave/Nebius model, not executable rate cards. Physical GPU density remains tranche-specific.

market.basis: One shared new-business curve using the existing Nebius 2027–30 house ladder ($18m/$19m/$20m/$21m per IT MW-year). Prices fix at modeled service commencement, not energisation. Current disclosures support improving pricing but do not establish these forward prices. Existing/inferred commitments retain their own rates through disclosed or estimated expiry. No quantified company software premium is assumed. The 2031 service-start price holds the 2030 level flat; it is a house extension, not a market quote.

limitations: Expiry quarters are estimates from modeled acceptance unless specifically marked disclosed.
An inferred existing-book allocation is not a verified customer commitment for that physical tranche.
Renewals do not retire or replace equipment. The long-run maintenance reserve is a separate house assumption.
Contract price by tenor is uncalibrated in the base case; the five-year discount is an explicit sensitivity.
Future prepayments and borrowing capacity are financing assumptions, not committed funding; customer credits follow modeled contract terms.
Delivery-delay tests retain the original capex purchase calendar. Fixed opening credit schedules remain unchanged.
Any prepayment balance without a credit calendar is deducted at face value at the horizon until its timing is sourced.
Forecast cash margin is 65%; normalized terminal margin is 65%.

Unmapped future tranches energizing from 2027Q1 use the shared new-business curve. Power leases do not establish customer compute prices. Existing and in-flight 2026 book and identifiable disclosed future commitments retain their own rates.
